manifest.name: Site Footer
manifest.description: Site-wide footer with the Rafters Studio brand mark, site-specific link columns, and a self-omitting ecosystem cross-link column.
manifest.solves: Consistent footer identity and link taxonomy across a multi-property product family, where each site cross-links its siblings but never itself, without forcing a JS runtime onto chrome.
appliesWhen: marketing or docs sites that belong to a shared product family
multi-property sites that need one ecosystem footer skinned per site
sites that want footer chrome themed through their own tokens

do: Column headings render through the Small primitive: uppercase, wider tracking, muted-foreground. The heading treatment is the composite's, not the site's.
The ecosystem (Projects) column is single-source inside the composite. Sites never pass their own Projects column.
The current site is omitted from the ecosystem column by its project key (the `current` input), not by host, because rafters.studio and mail.rafters.studio share the rafters.studio host.
Chrome stays zero-JS: assemble from Container + Grid + Small only. Theming flows from the consumer's tokens because the @/ imports resolve against the consumer at build time.
Per-site content arrives as leadingColumns (e.g. Docs, Internals) and a single siteColumn (the site's own resources: GitHub, llms.txt).
never: Hardcode or duplicate the ecosystem list per site. It lives once, in the composite.
Accept a Projects column through props. That column is owned by the composite.
Use any heading component other than Small for column labels.
Island React into the footer, or inline grid/flex utilities. Layout is Container + Grid.

input.name: leadingColumns
input.description: Site-specific columns shown before the ecosystem column, in order. Typically Docs and Internals.

input.name: siteColumn
input.description: The site's own resources column, shown after the ecosystem column. Heading is the product name; links are the site's GitHub, llms.txt, etc.
